Subject: FinCorp evals: next steps and dataset format

Hey Marissa / Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to align on our goals. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get the eval run on your side:

- Goal: validate model fit for FinCorp's customer support triage use case (intent classification + suggested response snippets).
- Priority metrics: intent accuracy (macro F1), suggestion relevance (human-rated 1-5), hallucination/unsafe output rate, avg latency (p50/p95), and cost per 1M tokens.
- Data: we have a 5k-sample export of historical tickets (anonymized) and a smaller human-annotated eval set (500 rows) we can share.

Requests:
1) Can you confirm the dataset format you need (CSV columns, prompt template)?
2) What models do you recommend we test first (and any quantized variants)?
3) How will Redwood run the scoring (automated metrics vs. human eval integration)?
4) Any concerns about PII retention or sandboxing on your side?

We'd like an initial public-facing benchmark and then a deeper FinCorp-specific eval. Target timeline: share dataset by EOD 28 Mar, kickoff next week.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Automation
FinCorp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinCorp evals: next steps and dataset format

Hi Alex — great to meet you today, and thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Dataset format: we prefer a CSV with one example per row. For your use case please include columns: id, customer_message, agent_response (optional), intent_label (if available), human_judgment (1-5) — see attached eval_dataset_template.csv. If you have multiple turns, include a conversation_id and turn_index.

2) Recommended models: for triage + short-response generation we typically start with a high-quality medium-latency variant and a fast low-cost variant to compare economics. Suggested initial set: 
   - Llama-2-70b-instruct (quantized Q4/8 for latency baseline)
   - Mistral-Instruct-8x (as a cost-efficient candidate)
   - Redwood-Chat-v1 (our curated generalist)
We can run both FP16 and quantized variants; we'll surface per-token latency and cost.

3) Scoring: automated metrics first (accuracy/F1, BLEU/ROUGE for snippets where appropriate) and then blended human ratings for relevance/hallucination. We'll provide a scoring template and can orchestrate a small human eval via your SMEs if you want. See scoring_guidelines.md attached.

4) PII / sandboxing: Redwood Private evals run in an isolated sandbox with ephemeral storage. We retain artifacts only for the duration of the eval unless you opt-in to longer retention. We support customer-managed keys for dataset encryption.

Attachments I'm including now: eval_dataset_template.csv, sample_prompt_set.md, scoring_guidelines.md, and a short initial-benchmark-results.pdf that shows comparatives on a public support dataset.

Next steps (proposed):
- You share the anonymized CSV by 2027-03-28.
- We provision a FinCorp eval workspace (sandbox) and run baseline models on a 500-sample subset within 3 business days.
- We share a results dashboard and a short write-up with recommendations (model choice, quantization, batching/caching config).

If that works I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for early next week (I'm flexible Tue/Wed mornings PST).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex — one additional note on scoring and dataset hygiene that may help speed onboarding:

- Prompt templates: use the sample_prompt_set.md. For intent classification we recommend a short system prompt + one-shot example. For response suggestion runs, include the preceding 1-2 turns in the prompt and cap generation at 128 tokens for parity across models.
- Scoring rubric: automated metrics we'll compute programmatically (macro F1 for intent; normalized BLEU/ROUGE for generated snippets). For human scoring, we ask reviewers to rate relevance (1-5) and mark any hallucinations or PII exposures. We'll produce a unified CSV with: id, model, generation, intent_pred, intent_confidence, automated_metrics, human_relevance, hallucination_flag, latency_ms, cost_usd.
- Pass/fail gating: we can run a quick regression check against your baseline (if you have one) and flag quality regressions >5% drop in macro F1 or >10% increase in hallucination rate.

Operational / logistics:
- Preferred upload: Google Drive link or S3 presigned URL.
- Sandbox visibility: we'll grant FinCorp reviewers read-only access to the results dashboard and raw outputs for verification.

I've attached scoring_guidelines.md with examples; happy to review with your SMEs on the kickoff call.

-Marissa
